profile.name: Alina Wu
profile.summary: Computer science student focused on human-centered design and software development. Interested in how people understand and use technology.

welcome.title: Alina
welcome.description: Computer Science at the University of Washington. Work across software and physical systems, with recurring attention to how people form expectations, make decisions, and interpret feedback.

readme.title: WORKSPACE NOTES
paragraphs: Read before reorganizing the lab. PROJECTS holds finished work. Working notes and unfinished ideas stay where they were last used.

Check the latest LAB LOG before picking up an old thread. Design decisions belong in the notebook, project sources in REFERENCES.web, physical iterations in the drawer, and open questions on the board. The bookshelf is reserved for personal reading and film notes.
Keep the unfinished parts in place. I may still need them. If I am away, leave comments beside the relevant material.

entries.title: Entering the Allen School
body: I'm excited to share that I will be joining the Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering at the University of Washington next quarter.
I will officially become a computer science student and continue building toward work in human-centered design and software development.

entries.title: Joining Thermo Fisher Scientific
body: I'm happy to share that I am joining Thermo Fisher Scientific as a Software Engineering Intern in Shanghai.
I will contribute to YOLO26-based vision for robot-assisted tube handling, 3500Dx localization testing, and QANTIS workflow analysis.

map.name: shanghai-map.case
map.title: Quality of Life in Shanghai
map.copy: Led an eight-person mixed-methods study of quality of life in older Shanghai neighborhoods. Translated the findings into a neighborhood-access map and community information campaigns.

details.label: FIELD RESEARCH
details.copy: Collected and analyzed 20+ questionnaires and interviews. The mixed-methods study examined neighborhood services, safety, and everyday information needs.

details.label: REPORTED FINDING
details.copy: An early 48-person questionnaire sample reported an average amenity-awareness score of 6.75 out of 10. This finding helped motivate the neighborhood-access map.

details.label: INTERACTIVE MAP
details.copy: Built a fixed-map prototype in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It organized nearby facilities by category and 5-, 10-, and 15-minute walking zones, with an early point-detail interaction.

details.label: COMMUNITY INTERVENTIONS
details.copy: Developed a food-safety poster addressing leftover-related misconceptions and an anti-fraud lecture for older residents. The presentation reported that 60.42% of respondents had not encountered anti-fraud publicity. Among those who had, 63.16% said it had not worked for them. Some participants later described the lecture as informative and clarifying.

allocation.name: course-allocation.py
allocation.title: Automatic and Satisfactory Course Assignment
allocation.copy: Independently designed and implemented a Python course-allocation system for capacity-constrained electives. The system uses ranked preferences to improve overall student satisfaction.

details.label: ALLOCATION METHOD
details.copy: Generated a fractional allocation through Simultaneous Eating. Birkhoff decomposition then converted it into possible final assignments.

details.label: SYSTEM STRUCTURE
details.copy: Separated preference generation, fractional allocation, deterministic realization, and evaluation into distinct Python stages.

details.label: REPORTED EVALUATION
details.copy: Tested the mechanism across 1,000 simulations with synthetically generated preferences and course capacities. The original presentation reported approximately 70% top-two and 92% top-three assignments.

details.label: EXTERNAL DISCUSSION
details.copy: Presented the project to 30+ professors and peers at the National Round of China Thinks Big. Discussions focused on possible applications and the need for real-world preference data.

details.label: LIVE DEPLOYMENT
details.copy: Adapted the framework for a class-wide parent–teacher meeting. The scheduler reduced manual planning, balanced attendance across time slots, and kept adjusted appointments close to parent preferences.

emg.name: emg-monitor.device
emg.title: Monitoring Device for Muscle Usage & Behavior
emg.copy: A wearable EMG device that measures relative target-muscle activation during exercise and summarizes each session across four intensity bands.

details.label: DESIGN DECISION
details.copy: Selected EMG over angular-displacement sensing for its ability to capture subtle muscle activity that was difficult to infer from visible surface movement.

details.label: CURRENT CHAIN
details.copy: A three-second calibration establishes an individual reference. The firmware filters and squares the EMG signal, then applies Kalman filtering. Each sample is assigned to one of four relative bands and included in the session summary.

details.label: PHYSICAL EVIDENCE
details.copy: Designed a two-part wearable enclosure in Fusion and AutoCAD for placement on the arm or leg. Its internal layout reserves compact spaces for the electronics, switch, and charging port.

details.label: CURRENT LIMIT
details.copy: The hardware prototype is operational. The software, data-analysis layer, and user interface remain in development.

research.title: Quantitative Analysis of Ethical-Case Survey Data
research.copy: Preparing participant survey data for ongoing research on case similarity, perceived relevance, and principle agreement.
research.quote: PYTHON / PANDAS / R / DATA TRANSFORMATION / REGRESSION

details.label: DATA PIPELINE
details.copy: Parsed comma-separated principle labels from survey responses. Counted and normalized each principle within its row, then assembled ordered vectors across the dataset.

details.label: RESEARCH WORKFLOW
details.copy: Used Python and pandas to prepare the data. Continued the analysis through spreadsheet formulas and linear models in R.

details.label: PRELIMINARY ANALYSIS
details.copy: Tested whether principle frequency predicted agreement. The current models did not detect a relationship for the principles examined.

details.label: CONTRIBUTION
details.copy: Developed the data-transformation workflow and contributed to empirical analysis using the lab's existing ethical-principle taxonomy.

internship.title: Software Engineering Internship
internship.copy: Work across robotic laboratory automation, localized scientific-software validation, workflow analysis for interface redesign, and technical onboarding.
internship.quote: YOLO26 / RGB-D / ROS2 / AGENTIC ENGINEERING / SOFTWARE TESTING

details.label: ROBOTIC TUBE HANDLING
details.copy: Developed a four-class YOLO26 perception pipeline for automated tube handling. Integrated RGB-D target localization with ROS2 chassis and robot-arm workflows for pickup and placement.

details.label: F1 / 3500Dx
details.copy: Executed black-box dynamic workflow test cases for F1 on the 3500Dx instrument. Clarified expected behavior and product workflows when test cases required additional context.

details.label: QANTIS
details.copy: Analyzed WinTrace, the previous EDXRF software. Documented page transitions and interaction paths in Miro to support the redesign.

details.label: INTERN ONBOARDING
details.copy: Onboarded a new intern to the testing environment. Set up the virtual machine, provided software training, resolved setup issues, and supported the transition to independent testing.
